100 Miles of Hope Blood Drive returns Nov. 2-4

By WBKO News Staff
Published: Nov. 2, 2026 at 5:20 PM EST|Updated: 11 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google

What This Story Is About

  • The annual 100 Miles of Hope Blood Drive between WKU and Middle Tennessee runs Nov. 2-4 at the Preston Health and Activities Center.

Why It Matters

  • All blood types are needed to ensure a reliable supply for patients.

What Happens Next

  • The winner will be announced Nov. 7 at WKU Football’s game at Middle Tennessee, where the American Red Cross will present the trophy.

For Context

  • The drive is annual and leads up to the Nov. 7 game. Appointments run 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. each day, and walk-ins are welcome.

BOWLING GREEN, Ky. (WBKO) - The annual 100 Miles of Hope Blood Drive against Middle Tennessee returns Monday, Nov. 2, through Wednesday, Nov. 4, leading up to WKU Football’s game at Middle Tennessee on Saturday, Nov. 7.

Donation location and times

Campus and community members are encouraged to schedule appointments to donate in favor of WKU at the Preston Health and Activities Center, 1906 College Heights Blvd., Bowling Green, Ky. 42101.

Appointments are available from 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. each day. Walk-ins are welcome, but scheduled appointments are encouraged.

Free parking spaces are available for community members scheduled to donate. Parking and donation details are available at wku.edu/blood-drive.

Winner announcement

The winner of the blood drive will be announced Nov. 7 at WKU Football’s game against Middle Tennessee at Johnny “Red” Floyd Stadium. The American Red Cross will present the trophy to the winning school.

Donor requirements

All blood types are needed to ensure a reliable supply for patients. Donors must present a blood donor card, a driver’s license or two other forms of identification at check-in.

Individuals who are 17 years old in most states (16 with parental consent where allowed by state law), weigh at least 110 pounds and are in generally good health may be eligible to donate. High school students and other donors 18 and younger also must meet certain height and weight requirements.

More information is available at wku.edu/blood-drive.
